newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia returns 114 boatpeople to China.
newsitem.headline: Australia returns 114 boatpeople to China.

text.p: The Australian government said on Sunday it had returned 114 boatpeople to China, reducing the number of illegal immigrants being held in a remote detention centre by about a third.

Australian Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock said in a statement those returned included a group of 70 who had been stranded off the Indonesian resort island of Lombok before being rescued on March 6 by a cattle ship off northern Australia.

Ruddock said none of those returned to China had qualified as "bona fide" refugees. Some had been held at the Port Hedland detention camp on the north-western coast of Australia for more than two years.
"When illegal immigrants arrive in Australia they will be sent home immediately if they do not have a claim to remain here," Ruddock said.

"It was unfortunate that some of the...illegal immigrants sent back at the weekend had been in detention for longer periods. Many had been involved in extensive litigation that had ultimately proved fruitless," he said.
Ruddock added that 161 mainly ethnic Chinese remained in detention at Port Hedland.
